reader.requirement: At --std 85 a USAGE clause (BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL/COMP, DISPLAY, INDEX, PACKED-DECIMAL) must be accepted in every data description entry of level 01-49 or 77 in every section, and refused in a level-66 (RENAMES) or level-88 (condition-name) entry.
reader.edition-search: Read LevelNumberPass (its doc states it is not edition-gated: every level/format set is the same in all editions) and grepped LevelNumberPass.cs, CobolData.g4 dataDescriptionBody/renamesClause/usageClause for CobolVersion, IsAtLeast, Edition.Is, ConstructRegistry, DialectBehavior, semantic predicates: none on this path. The grammar keeps renamesClause an alternative to the clause list, so USAGE cannot be written with RENAMES; an 88 body that is not value-only is refused by CheckEntryFormat at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f10_01 covers USAGE on 77, 01 and 05/10 working-storage entries; it does not exercise the refusal half (66 and 88) nor the file and linkage sections

probes.printed: COBOL1747 level-number 88 on 'B-OK': ... this entry's body is not a value clause alone (88 B-OK USAGE COMP VALUE 1)
probes.expected: refused: USAGE not allowed on level 88

probes.printed: COBOL1941 unexpected 'RENAMES' ... not a clause of the data description entry for 'R' (66 R USAGE DISPLAY RENAMES A THRU B)
probes.expected: refused: USAGE not allowed on level 66

probes.printed: COBOL0001 unexpected 'USAGE' (66 R RENAMES A THRU B USAGE DISPLAY)
probes.expected: refused: USAGE not allowed on level 66

probes.printed: -1234 -12345 +123456 XYZ -999 / -0012 007 / TX3 (FD record with COMPUTATIONAL, PACKED-DECIMAL, BINARY, DISPLAY and a USAGE COMP subgroup written and read back sequentially; 77 COMP; 01 group USAGE DISPLAY; 01 USAGE INDEX set from an index)
probes.expected: accepted in the file and working-storage sections and values preserved through WRITE/READ

probes.printed: COBOL0900 a fixed-width binary usage (BINARY-CHAR/-SHORT/-LONG/-DOUBLE) requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85) for 01 D BINARY-LONG

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR1  (5.14.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: USAGE on 88 is refused by LevelNumberPass's format arm (the body is not a value clause alone); USAGE on 66 is a parse refusal because renamesClause is an alternative body, not a clause in the list. Both are edition-invariant. The diagnostics cite §2023 text, but the 1985 requirement is met.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR1 (cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.14.3 SR1  (5.14.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1) and §1985:VI.5.7.4 GR2b (OK). Probes at --std 85 under refute-1985-224/src: u5a.cob (USAGE on an SD 01 record and a FILLER subordinate, a level-49 COMPUTATIONAL leaf nine groups deep, a 01 REDEFINES with PACKED-DECIMAL, a 01 FILLER USAGE BINARY group, USAGE INDEX at 01 and under OCCURS, linkage 77 COMP and 01 PACKED-DECIMAL group) exit 0, printed -0007 0012 / OK; r5d.cob (CD record entry with USAGE COMP) reached no USAGE diagnostic (only the expected CD-size and ODO errors); u5b.cob (2002 usages NATIONAL, POINTER, FLOAT-LONG, BIT, PROGRAM-POINTER) each refused COBOL0900 at 85. COMP-5 and COMP-1 are accepted at 85 without a diagnostic: that is the general format's closed list of usages under the extension flag, not SR1's level-number placement, so it does not bear on this rule. The reader's 66 and 88 refusals (u1a, u1b, u1c) stand; no edition site on the path (grep of LevelNumberPass.cs for CobolVersion/IsAtLeast/Edition.Is/ConstructRegistry/DialectBehavior/ReservedWords: none).
